answer: Sybil resistance for AI agents rests on per-identity stake that can be slashed. Each agent posts a lotus-sized bond in escrow, forfeited in full if its behaviour is traced to duplicates. Reputation cannot be copied across identifiers, so an attacker minting ten thousand personas must fund ten thousand separate deposits. Because honest reward per task is capped below that stake, a fake identity needs a gale of non-replicable work before profit appears. A jade-tier fee on first payout raises marginal cost again, so registration cost scales linearly with fake agents while payoff stays flat.
